title: Duroply Industries Ltd - 516003 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Duroply Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record ₹122.2 crore (+17% YoY) and EBITDA margin rose to 7.1%, with PAT of ₹4.38 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 was the company's highest quarterly revenue to date at ₹122.2 crore, up 17% YoY and 22.7% QoQ, delivering on the double-digit growth guidance given in Q1. Profit before tax rose 82% YoY to ₹4.86 crore and EBITDA rose 33.4% to ₹8.62 crore, with margin expanding to 7.1% as operating expenses were held roughly flat. Gross margin dipped slightly to 34.6% on higher raw material costs. Management also launched a new MDF product (Duro HDMMR) on an asset-light basis and reported improved working capital.

financial_highlights.change: +17% YoY; +22.7% QoQ; highest quarterly revenue to date (previous best ₹111.6 crore in Q4 FY26)
+33.4% YoY; +79% QoQ; margin vs 6.2% last year and 4.8% in Q1
vs ~34.8% last year and 35.5% in Q1
+12% YoY; in-house ₹114 crore, contract manufacturing ₹107.8 crore
Debtor days 38 (vs 42 in FY26); inventory days 151 (vs 164 in Q1, 145 in FY26); creditor days 88 (vs 72 in FY26)

segments.name: In-house manufactured goods
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹62.7 crore, up 18.5% YoY and 22% QoQ; H1 revenue ₹114 crore.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue ₹59.5 crore, up 15.4% YoY and 23% QoQ; H1 revenue ₹107.8 crore.

segments.name: MDF (Duro HDMMR, new category)
segments.commentary: Launched in the quarter on an asset-light model with no company capex, leveraging a third party's capacity; management called it a small start with response in line with expectations.

guidance_outlook: Management expects double-digit revenue growth for FY27 and H2 FY27 to be better than H1.
Margins expected to be sustainable over the next two quarters if raw material and chemical costs do not rise further.
Brand spend to stay disciplined, with returns tracked; Q2 brand spend 3.6% of sales vs 3.9% in Q1 and 2.7% for last year overall.
Near-term risk to H2 growth flagged in Delhi/NCR from construction challenges at this time of year.
capex_capacity: Modernisation of the Rajkot plant is progressing well; no timeline or capex amount given.
MDF entry (Duro HDMMR) is asset-light with no company capex; capacity is sourced from a third party with overcapacity in the industry.
No further MDF product launches planned for now; focus is on the high-density line for retail demand.
demand_pricing: Q1 was described as a blip, with challenges in April and May; growth has been on track since.
Strong brand position in northern India, with the company positioned as retail-focused rather than institutional.
Raw material inflation: shipping rates and chemical costs have not eased and are rising, the main concern on pricing and pass-through to customers.
Employee cost flat at about 10.4% of sales (12.8% in Q1); operating expenses 27.5% of revenue (28.9% prior year).

qa_highlights.question: What drove the 7.1% EBITDA margin and is it sustainable over the next two quarters and next year?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin gain came from higher revenue over flat overheads, with COGS similar to Q1 apart from a minor dip from raw material inflation. Management expects margins to hold over the next six months if input costs stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: Why enter MDF now, given management earlier indicated no new segments for 12-18 months, and given larger MDF peers are struggling with overcapacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Entry is asset-light with no capex, using a partner's idle capacity. The company sees a gap in its northern India project and site network, where MDF/HDMMR is used on most sites. Response is at par with expectations.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company add more MDF products?
qa_highlights.answer: Focus is on the high-density product line given retail demand; more products will be considered only after establishing the current line and if product line extension opportunities emerge.

risks_watch: Raw material and chemical costs, plus shipping rates, are rising and could compress gross margin if not passed on to customers.
Delhi/NCR construction slowdown expected in the coming months may affect H2 growth.
Brand spend has risen over the last two quarters; returns on that spend need tracking.
Early-stage MDF business with limited scale; dependence on third-party capacity.
Inventory days at 151 remain high, though down from 164 in Q1.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on Q2 delivery and H2 outlook, with the caveat that raw material cost uncertainty is the main concern. Answers on MDF entry were direct, while the margin sustainability answer was conditional on input costs.
key_quotes: Let me begin with the major headline, Q2 FY27 was our strongest quarter so far.
The challenge really right now is there's way too much uncertainty on the raw material cost and how much of that we would be able to actually pass on to our customers.
Our entry into this segment is on an asset-light model. There is no CapEx from the company.

adds.what: Rajkot plant modernisation (no capacity number, timeline or capex given)

growth.why: Management is "very optimistic" of double-digit FY27 growth (guided ~10%+), with H2 expected better than H1, but backing is aspirational: demand recovery in retail-focused north India and an asset-light MDF launch with no capex or capacity numbers, plus an unquantified Rajkot modernisation.

quality.why: Q2 revenue rose 17% YoY to ₹122.2 crore, with both in-house (+18.5%) and contract manufacturing (+15.4%) growing, and the brief cites no one-off gains, low base, or acquisitions; the main caveat is that the brief does not say whether growth was volume or price, so the driver is recorded as volume only on the basis of unit-count language being absent, which makes it a soft call.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: EBITDA margin hit 7.1% in Q2 (vs 4.8% in Q1, 6.2% last year) on flat opex at 27.5% of revenue, and management expects it to hold for six months only if raw material and chemical costs stop rising, which they have not.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No new plant, line or capacity number was guided; Rajkot modernisation has no timeline or capex amount, and MDF is sourced from a third party's idle capacity with no company capex.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Q2 revenue of ₹122.2 crore was up 17% YoY and 22.7% QoQ, H1 was up 12%, and management guided double-digit FY27 growth with H2 better than H1, though Delhi/NCR construction slowdown is a risk.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex utilisation was not disclosed and no new capex was discussed beyond the unquantified Rajkot modernisation, with the MDF entry deliberately asset-light.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management only reiterated double-digit FY27 growth (about 10%+) and did not signal a raise, while H1 revenue growth was 12% and raw material inflation is a headwind.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Raw material, chemical and shipping costs are still rising, which could compress the 34.6% gross margin, and Delhi/NCR construction slowdown is a flagged H2 risk to growth.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Duro HDMMR MDF launched in Q2 already, and management said no further MDF launches are planned for now, with focus on the high-density line.

rows.label: MDF (Duro HDMMR) asset-light entry in northern India
rows.why: Launched in the quarter on a third-party's idle capacity with no company capex, and management called response in line with expectations though the business is still small.

rows.label: Inventory and cash cycle improvement
rows.why: Inventory days fell to 151 from 164 in Q1 and 145 in FY26 (still high), debtor days fell to 38 from 42, and cash conversion cycle is 101 days, so further release is plausible but inventory is still elevated.

rows.label: Brand spend discipline
rows.why: Brand spend was 3.6% of sales in Q2 vs 3.9% in Q1, but it has risen over the last two quarters and returns on it still need tracking.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q2 delivery, H2 outlook and the MDF entry, but conditional on raw material costs for margin sustainability; analysts pushed on why enter MDF despite prior no-new-segment comments and peer overcapacity.
